title_en: Jinxi County People's Procuratorate of Jiangxi Province v. Xu Huawen and Fang Yuping — civil public interest litigation for protection of cultural relics
ruling_gist_en: Where damage to ecological resources is caused by the destruction of ancient monuments, architectural complexes, sites, and other cultural relics, the tortfeasor shall bear tort liability. The procuratorial authority may, in accordance with law, initiate environmental civil public interest litigation against cases where damage to ecological resources is caused by destruction of cultural relics. In the absence of an appraisal by an appraisal institution on the loss of human ecological resources caused by damage to ancient buildings, expert opinions that have been cross-examined in court may serve as the basis for determination. The people's court shall comprehensively consider the procuratorial authority's public interest litigation claims, the economic development level of the location of the cultural relics, the social influence of the cultural relics themselves, the defendant's subjective fault and economic conditions, the degree of damage to the integrity of the cultural relics, and expert opinions, and shall determine the loss of human ecological resources at its discretion in accordance with law.

full_text_en:
Jinxi County People's Procuratorate, Jiangxi Province v. Xu Huawen and Fang Yuping

— Civil Public Interest Litigation for the Protection of Human Relics

Ruling Summary

Where damage to ecological resources is caused by the destruction of human relics such as historic sites, building complexes, or ruins, the tortfeasor shall bear tort liability. The procuratorate may, in accordance with the law, initiate environmental civil public interest litigation in cases involving damage to ecological resources caused by the destruction of human relics. In the absence of an appraisal by an appraisal institution on the loss of human ecological resources caused by damage to ancient buildings, expert opinions that have been subjected to in-court cross-examination may serve as the basis for factual determination. The people's court shall, taking into comprehensive consideration factors such as the claims in the public interest litigation initiated by the procuratorate, the level of economic development of the locality where the human relics are located, the social influence of the human relics themselves, the subjective fault of the defendant and the defendant's economic conditions, the extent of destruction to the integrity of the human relics, and expert opinions, determine the loss of human ecological resources in accordance with the law and in its discretion.

Plaintiff in the Public Interest Litigation: Jinxi County People's Procuratorate, Jiangxi Province.

Defendant: Xu Huawen, male, born on December 7, 1969, Han Chinese, residing in Jinxi County, Jiangxi Province.

Defendant: Fang Yuping, male, born on March 12, 1966, Han Chinese, residing in Jinxi County, Jiangxi Province.

The Jinxi County People's Procuratorate, Jiangxi Province, filed a public prosecution against Xu Huawen, Fang Yuping, and others for the crime of theft by an indictment (Jin Jian Xing Su [2020] No. 174) with the Jinxi County People's Court, Jiangxi Province, on January 5, 2021. The Jinxi County People's Court rendered a criminal judgment ( [2021] Gan 1027 Xing Chu No. 8 ) on May 7, 2021, finding Xu Huawen and Fang Yuping guilty of theft, sentencing them to fixed-term imprisonment of one year and four months and one year and three months, respectively, and imposing a fine of RMB 10,000 on each. The Jinxi County People's Procuratorate notified the relevant case information on December 17, 2020. During the notification period, no organ or relevant organization stipulated by law initiated civil public interest litigation. On January 22, 2021, the Jinxi County People's Procuratorate initiated ancillary civil public interest litigation for the protection of human relics with the Jinxi County People's Court.

Jinxi County People's Procuratorate, Jiangxi Province, alleged in its complaint: At around 9:00 p.m. on April 11, 2020, the defendants Xu Huawen and Fang Yuping drove a three-wheeled motorcycle to a gateway building in Xi'an Group, Boyuan Village, Liuli Township, Jinxi County, and stole a stone plaque inscribed with "Jia Di Li" (First Class in the Imperial Examinations Residence). During the theft, the defendants caused the stone plaque to fall and break. The defendants then loaded the broken stone plaque onto the vehicle and transported it back to Yunshan Town. Boyuan Village, Liuli Township, is a traditional village of Jiangxi Province, possessing relatively rich tangible and intangible cultural heritage, and having regional cultural characteristics and the style of a traditional village. The "Jia Di Li" gateway building involved in this case constitutes a non-renewable ancient architectural resource and is an integral part of Boyuan Village, possessing corresponding historical, cultural, and economic value. The theft and damage of the plaque on this gateway building altered the original style of the ancient building, severed the original historical and cultural inheritance, and to a certain extent accelerated the demise of the ancient building, impairing its historical, cultural, and economic value and infringing upon the public interest. According to an assessment by the Fujian Branch of Chongqing Engineering Design Institute, the cost of repairing the "Jia Di Li" gateway building was RMB 9,812.

On the night of April 27, 2020, Xu Huawen and Fang Yuping drove a three-wheeled motorcycle to a gateway building in Xiayang Group, Hufang Village, Heshizhen, and stole a stone plaque inscribed with "San Gong Jiu Di" (Former Residence of Three Dukes). During the theft, the defendants caused the stone plaque to break and the gateway building to collapse entirely. The defendants then loaded the broken stone plaque onto the vehicle and transported it back to Yunshan Town. Shanke Village and Zhongling Village, which are under the jurisdiction of Hufang Village, Heshizhen, are traditional Chinese villages. Xiayang Group, Hufang Village, is relatively close in spatial distance to Shanke Village and Zhongling Village, and shares similar historical and cultural inheritance and styles, all possessing certain regional cultural characteristics and the style of a traditional village. The "San Gong Jiu Di" gateway building involved in this case carries certain historical, cultural, artistic, social, and economic value, and has certain historical reference value for researching the ancient architectural clusters of the Ming and Qing Dynasties in Jinxi County and the farming culture of Jiangxi. The theft of the plaque and the severe damage to the entire gateway building caused historical, cultural, and economic losses, impairing the public interest. According to an assessment by the Fujian Branch of Chongqing Engineering Design Institute, the cost of repairing the "San Gong Jiu Di" gateway building was RMB 93,727.61. Xu Huawen sold the two stolen stone plaques to Huang Guangchun for a total of RMB 2,200. According to an expert assessment, the acts of Xu Huawen and Fang Yuping in stealing the architectural components of the ancient buildings caused a total loss of human ecological environment service functions amounting to RMB 310,617.

The theft by defendants Xu Huawen and Fang Yuping severely damaged the historical, artistic, and cultural value of the stolen gateway buildings, impaired the public interest, and has not yet restored them to their original condition or compensated for the losses up to the present. Therefore, they shall bear corresponding civil tort liability. The claims were as follows: 1. The two defendants shall bear the repair cost of RMB 9,812 for the "Jia Di Li" gateway building and RMB 93,727.61 for the "San Gong Jiu Di" gateway building, totaling RMB 103,539.61; 2. The two defendants shall bear the loss of human ecological environment service functions amounting to RMB 310,617; 3. The two defendants shall bear appraisal costs totaling RMB 11,200.

Defendant Xu Huawen argued in his defense: The appraisal opinion was not issued by a state cultural relics appraisal institution or by a cultural relics appraisal and evaluation personnel registered with the State Administration of Cultural Heritage; the expert appraisal opinion lacked scientific basis. Xu Huawen is a farmer who was completely unaware of the non-renewable nature of cultural relics, and his family faces financial difficulties. His degree of subjective fault and ability to pay compensation should be fully considered. He requested the court to render a fair judgment on the loss of human ecological environment service functions after ordering the payment of repair costs.

Defendant Fang Yuping argued in his defense: Fang Yuping expressed regret for the damage caused to cultural, historical, and artistic value by his wrongful conduct and was willing to compensate for relevant economic losses within the statutory scope and carry out repairs. The loss of human ecological environment service functions of RMB 310,617 constitutes compensation for moral damages, which is an indirect economic loss and should not be supported. The two experts lacked the subject-matter qualification to issue statutory appraisal opinions, the procedure for issuing the opinions was unlawful, the opinions lacked statutory data basis and specialized industry regulations, and they could not be used as the sole basis for deciding the case. Fang Yuping was unaware that his conduct would cause such significant damage to the cultural, historical, and artistic value of the gateway building, and his family's financial means are limited. Fang Yuping was willing to bear the repair costs and appraisal costs totaling over RMB 100,000, and he had already received education and punishment.

The Jinxi County People's Court, Jiangxi Province, found the following facts at the first instance:

Boyuan Village, Liuli Township, Jinxi County, is a "traditional village of Jiangxi Province," possessing rich tangible and intangible cultural heritage. At approximately 9:00 p.m. on April 11, 2020, the defendants Xu Huawen and Fang Yuping drove a three-wheeled motorcycle to a gateway building in Xi'an Group, Boyuan Village, and stole a stone plaque inscribed with "Jia Di Li." During the theft, they caused the stone plaque to fall and break. On the night of April 27 of the same year, the two defendants drove a three-wheeled motorcycle to a gateway building in Xiayang Group and stole a stone plaque inscribed with "San Gong Jiu Di." During the theft, they caused the stone plaque to break and the gateway building to collapse entirely. During this period, the two defendants loaded the two broken stone plaques onto the vehicle and transported them to Yunshan Town, Linchuan District, Fuzhou City, where they sold them to another person for RMB 2,200. The two stone plaques have not been recovered.

According to an assessment by a professional institution, the cost of repairing the "Jia Di Li" gateway building was RMB 9,812, and the cost of repairing the "San Gong Jiu Di" gateway building was RMB 93,727.61. According to an expert assessment, the acts of the two defendants in stealing the architectural components of the ancient buildings caused a total loss of human ecological environment service functions amounting to RMB 310,617.

It was also found that Jinxi County is one of the "Top Ten Ancient Cultural Counties of Jiangxi," possessing 7 famous historical and cultural towns (villages) designated at the national level, 128 traditional villages, and 11,633 ancient buildings from the Ming and Qing Dynasties, including 42 traditional Chinese villages and 31 traditional villages of Jiangxi Province, and is hailed as "a museum of ancient villages without walls."

The Jinxi County People's Court, Jiangxi Province, held at the first instance:

Human relics fall within the scope of protection under China's environmental law. Traditional villages are valuable cultural heritage left by China's farming civilization, belong to human relics, and are an important component of the environment. The protection of traditional villages should emphasize the protection of their ecological and cultural value. At the same time, the protection of traditional villages must focus on holistic protection in order to achieve the sustainable development of traditional villages. Where damage to ecological resources is caused by the destruction of human relics such as historic sites, building complexes, or ruins, the tortfeasor shall bear tort liability. The plaques inscribed with "Jia Di Li" and "San Gong Jiu Di" and the buildings to which they are attached, involved in this case, possess strong regional cultural characteristics and contain rich historical information, and are non-renewable cultural heritage.

This case is an ecological protection case among environmental resources cases. The plaintiff in the public interest litigation sued the two defendants to bear civil tort liability. Regarding the tortious act and the causal relationship between the tortious act and the harmful consequences, the fact that the theft by the two defendants caused damage to the stolen gateway buildings has been confirmed by the effective criminal judgment. Therefore, the focus of the trial in this case is: 1. Whether the procuratorate can initiate environmental civil public interest litigation for acts of destroying traditional villages. 2. In the absence of an appraisal institution capable of appraising the loss of human ecological resources caused by damage to ancient buildings, whether expert opinions issued by persons with specialized knowledge can be admitted as evidence. 3. How to determine the losses in this case. The analysis is as follows:

1. Regarding whether the procuratorate can initiate environmental civil public interest litigation for acts of destroying traditional villages.

Boyuan Village, Liuli Township, Jinxi County, is a "traditional village of Jiangxi Province," possessing rich tangible and intangible cultural heritage. The "Jia Di Li" gateway building is a non-renewable ancient architectural resource. The theft and damage of the plaque on this gateway building altered the original style of the ancient building and severed the original historical and cultural inheritance. Xiayang Group, Hufang Village, Heshizhen, Jinxi County, is close in distance to the "traditional Chinese villages" Shanke Village and Zhongling Village, and possesses regional cultural characteristics and the style of a traditional village. The "San Gong Jiu Di" gateway building carries certain historical, cultural, artistic, social, and economic value, and has certain historical reference value for researching the local ancient architectural clusters of the Ming and Qing Dynasties and the farming culture of Jiangxi. The court held that human relics fall under cultural heritage. Although cultural heritage belongs to the spiritual civilization category, it is manifested through certain material carriers. Traditional villages are a composite of tangible cultural heritage and intangible cultural heritage. The theft and damage of the aforementioned gateway plaques severely damaged the ecological value and historical-cultural value of the stolen gateway buildings, impairing the public interest. The losses caused in this case include both direct economic losses, which are intuitive and direct, such as the cost of repairing the gateway plaques, and intangible ecological and humanistic value losses. The two defendants shall bear corresponding civil tort liability. This case involves the protection of the public interest in ecological resources. Where no organ or organization stipulated by law initiates litigation, the procuratorate may initiate environmental civil public interest litigation.

2. Regarding whether, in the absence of an appraisal institution capable of appraising the loss of human ecological resources caused by damage to ancient buildings, expert opinions issued by persons with specialized knowledge can be admitted as evidence.

In this case, because no appraisal institution could appraise the loss of human ecological resources, two experts were commissioned to issue the "Expert Appraisal Opinion." Upon examination, the two experts were: Ding Chaokang, Associate Research Librarian of the Fuzhou City Cultural Relics Protection Center, and Cheng Xiaohui, Associate Research Librarian of the Fuzhou City Museum. Both were cultural relics and museum experts, possessing specialized knowledge in the field of cultural relics and museums, and had long been engaged in research in the field of cultural relics protection. They had the ability to evaluate specialized issues such as damage to human ecological resources caused by damage to ancient buildings, and thus qualified as "persons with specialized knowledge." The two experts, commissioned by the plaintiff in the public interest litigation, relying on their professional knowledge and consulting materials, after full discussion and analysis, gave clear professional opinions on the functional damage caused by the damage to the ancient buildings from the perspective of human ecological environment, and appeared in court as experts to answer questions from the parties and the adjudicators. According to Article 79 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China: "A party may apply to the people's court to notify a person with specialized knowledge to appear in court to give opinions on the appraisal opinion made by the appraiser or on professional issues." Article 122 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates: "A party may, in accordance with Article 79 of the Civil Procedure Law, apply before the expiration of the举证 period for one or two persons with specialized knowledge to appear in court to represent the party in cross-examining the appraisal opinion or to give opinions on professional issues involved in the facts of the case. The opinions given by a person with specialized knowledge on professional issues in court shall be deemed as statements of the party." Article 15 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases stipulates: "Where a party applies to notify a person with specialized knowledge to appear in court to give opinions on specialized issues such as the appraisal opinion made by the appraiser, or on causation, ecological environment restoration methods, ecological environment restoration costs, and losses caused by the loss of service functions during the period from the damage to the ecological environment to the completion of restoration, the people's court may permit it. The expert opinions referred to in the preceding paragraph, after cross-examination, may serve as the basis for finding the facts." The court held that the issuing主体 and formation procedure of the "Expert Appraisal Opinion" were lawful. The opinions issued by the two experts, after full discussion and analysis, had clear conclusions, and were subjected to in-court cross-examination. They possessed legality and scientific validity, complied with the provisions of the aforementioned laws and judicial interpretations, and could serve as the basis for finding the facts in this case in accordance with the law.

3. Regarding how to determine the losses in this case.

The theft of the gateway plaques in this case also caused damage to the buildings to which they were attached. According to the restoration design for the buildings to which the two plaques were attached made by the Fujian Branch of Chongqing Engineering Design Institute, which possesses the qualification for cultural relics engineering design, the restoration budget for the "Jia Di Li" gateway building was RMB 9,812, and the restoration budget for the "San Gong Jiu Di" gateway building was RMB 93,727.61. The court held that the above restoration costs were appraisal opinions made by a qualified professional institution, and the two defendants had no objection to these restoration costs. Therefore, the court supported the claim of the plaintiff in the public interest litigation that the two defendants should bear the repair cost of RMB 9,812 for the "Jia Di Li" gateway building and RMB 93,727.61 for the "San Gong Jiu Di" gateway building.

Regarding the determination of the loss of human ecological resources. The court held that the plaintiff in the public interest litigation's claim that the two defendants should bear the loss of human ecological environment service functions essentially required the two defendants to bear the loss of human ecological resources caused. This includes both the loss of service functions and the loss of permanent functions. Therefore, the court defined the losses caused in this case as the loss of human ecological resources. The plaques inscribed with "Jia Di Li" and "San Gong Jiu Di" and the buildings to which they are attached, involved in this case, possess strong regional cultural characteristics and contain rich historical information, and are non-renewable cultural heritage. Although the stolen plaques and the damaged gateway buildings could be restored to their original appearance, the original stolen plaques are difficult to recover, and the human ecological value of the restored gateway buildings and plaques will inevitably be diminished compared to the original. The integrity of the original ecological traditional village style and the inheritance function of the traditional village's history and culture have been irreversibly damaged, causing damage to the local human ecological resources. This damage has seriously affected the humanistic feelings and historical emotions of the local people. Such intangible losses are difficult to measure in monetary terms. Taking into comprehensive consideration the level of local economic development in Jinxi County, the fact that Boyuan Village, where the "Jia Di Li" stone plaque was located, is a "traditional village of Jiangxi Province," the subjective fault of the two defendants and their family economic conditions, the extent of destruction to the integrity of the traditional village, and the opinion of the experts who issued the loss of human ecological environment service functions of RMB 310,617 based on their professional knowledge, and in accordance with Article 21 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases, which provides that "Where the plaintiff claims compensation from the defendant for losses caused by the loss of service functions during the period from the damage to the ecological environment to the completion of restoration, and for losses caused by permanent damage to ecological environment functions, the people's court may support it in accordance with the law," the court, in its discretion, determined that the two defendants should bear losses caused by the destruction of human ecological resources amounting to RMB 300,000. The appraisal and assessment costs totaling RMB 11,200 shall be borne by the two defendants jointly.

Human relics carry splendid civilization, inherit history and culture, and sustain the national spirit. Jinxi County, as one of the "Top Ten Ancient Cultural Counties of Jiangxi," possesses numerous traditional villages and ancient buildings. The trial of this case is not only a negative evaluation of the conduct of the two defendants and a remedy for the impairment of the rights and interests of the general public in human ecological resources, but also serves to warn, educate, and awaken the awareness of all members of society regarding the protection of human ecological resources, enhance the consciousness of protecting non-renewable cultural heritage such as the style of traditional villages and ancient buildings, and better preserve historical inheritance and beautiful nostalgia.

In accordance with these findings, the Jinxi County People's Court, Jiangxi Province, pursuant to Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Temporal Effect of the Application of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, Articles 1165, 1168, 1229, and 1235 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, Articles 2 and 64 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 15, 18, 20, 21, 22, and 23 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases, Articles 55 and 79 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 122 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on December 31, 2021:

1. Defendants Xu Huawen and Fang Yuping shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect, jointly and severally compensate for the repair cost of the "Jia Di Li" gateway building in the amount of RMB 9,812, and the repair cost of the "San Gong Jiu Di" gateway building in the amount of RMB 93,727.61, totaling repair costs of RMB 103,539.61;

2. Defendants Xu Huawen and Fang Yuping shall, within thirty days from the date this judgment takes legal effect, jointly and severally compensate for the loss of human ecological resources in the amount of RMB 300,000;

3. Defendants Xu Huawen and Fang Yuping shall bear the appraisal and assessment costs of RMB 11,200.

After the judgment was pronounced at the first instance, none of the parties appealed, and the judgment of the first instance has taken legal effect.
